title: What an AI assistant is good and bad at
point: An AI assistant is excellent at working with words you give it, and unreliable at facts, sums and anything it cannot see.
definition: An AI assistant, such as Copilot or ChatGPT, is a tool that predicts likely text in reply to your request. It writes fluent language quickly, but fluent does not mean correct.

objective.text: Given eight workplace tasks, classify each as a good fit or a poor fit for an AI assistant and name the weakness behind every poor fit.

misconceptions.claim: The assistant looks things up in a trusted database, so its facts are reliable.
misconceptions.correction: Unless it is connected to a search or company documents, it generates answers from patterns it learned. It can produce a confident, specific and completely wrong fact.

misconceptions.claim: If the assistant can write a polished report, it can also do the maths in it.
misconceptions.correction: Writing and calculating are different skills. Assistants often slip on arithmetic, percentages and totals, so check every number with a calculator or spreadsheet.

l1: An AI assistant is strong at four jobs: drafting new text, summarising long text, reformatting text into another shape, and brainstorming options.
It is weak at four things: facts with no source, maths, recent events, and anything it cannot see, such as your inbox or your team's private files.
A hallucination is an answer that sounds right but is made up. It is the main reason the weak areas matter.
l2: Priya in HR needs to turn a two-page leave policy into a short staff FAQ. That is summarising and reformatting, which suits an assistant well.
She also wants to know how many leave days the average employee took last year. The assistant cannot see the HR system, so any figure it gives would be invented.
The useful split is clear: let the assistant draft the FAQ, and pull the leave figure from the HR report herself.
l3: Suppose drafting a weekly client update takes you 40 minutes by hand and 10 minutes with an assistant, plus 10 minutes of checking.
You save 20 minutes a week, about 16 hours a year. That is worth it because the checking time is included in the sum.
Now suppose the task is a weekly sales total. Checking it fully takes as long as doing it, so the assistant saves nothing and adds risk.
